articles.title: Forty Hours on a Bus, Thirteen Visas Denied, Zero Tickets for Fans. Iran Made It to the World Cup Anyway.

articles.title: He Was Hit on the Helmet. He Vomited on the Pitch. He Hit the Winning Six Anyway.
articles.excerpt: Bangladesh captain Mehidy Hasan Miraz batted through a concussion to seal his country's first-ever ODI series victory over Australia — a result 21 years in the making.
articles.image_caption: Bangladesh captain Mehidy Hasan Miraz during a cricket match
articles.nri_angle: Bangladesh's first-ever ODI series win over Australia, sealed by a captain who batted through a concussion, is a landmark moment for the Bangladeshi diaspora and South Asian cricket fans worldwide.

articles.title: Jaspal Rana, India's Greatest Commonwealth Games Athlete and Manu Bhaker's Coach, Dies at 49
articles.excerpt: The pistol shooting legend and Dronacharya Award-winning coach suffered a fatal cardiac emergency after falling ill during the ISSF World Cup in Munich
articles.image_caption: Jaspal Rana in 2007, during his years as one of India's most decorated pistol shooters
articles.image_credit: Government of India, GODL-India, via Wikimedia Commons
articles.nri_angle: Jaspal Rana was among the first Indian athletes to achieve sustained international dominance outside cricket, becoming an icon for millions of NRIs who followed his Commonwealth and Asian Games campaigns through the 1990s and 2000s. His protégée Manu Bhaker's Paris Olympics double bronze was a defining moment for diaspora sports fans worldwide.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Red Cards, a Nine-Minute Opener, and a Son Heung-min Substitution. Day 1 of the World Cup Had Everything.

articles.nri_angle: With 104 matches across 16 venues in the US, Canada, and Mexico, this is the first World Cup NRIs in North America can attend in their own backyard.

articles.title: Sixteen Teams. Five Weeks. And India Open Against Pakistan on Sunday. The Women's T20 World Cup Starts Today.

articles.title: They Scored 349. It Wasn't Enough. Rain and DLS Handed Afghanistan A a Stunning Win in Dambulla.

articles.title: He Is Thirty-Nine. On Saturday, He Will Become the Oldest Indian to Play an ODI.

articles.title: Nine Fours. Zero Sixes. The Most Important Innings of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's Life.

articles.title: He Loaded Up to Bowl. Then He Stopped. Arjun Tendulkar Refused to Mankad.

articles.nri_angle: For NRIs who grew up watching Sachin Tendulkar embody the 'spirit of cricket,' seeing his son make the same choice — sportsmanship over the rulebook, in a semi-final, at the same Wankhede Stadium where Sachin built his legend — feels like watching a value system pass from one generation to the next.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
